mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of months with positive PAYEMS growth, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that accelerates economic growth and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS>4.5% and CPIAUCSL>199.0, or the Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of months during monetary tightening cycles, or the average return in tightening cycles is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) reflects strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of months with rising HOUST, or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 2,200 thousand units, it signals robust economic growth and strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of months with HOUST>2200.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates a weakening supply chain and economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO and GDPC1 both decline, or the Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of industrial contraction (as indicated by INDPRO below 110.0), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate output and earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of months with INDPRO<110.0, or the average return in contraction periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
